title: This 150-Million-Year-Old Bird Had a Body Built for the Land - Nautilus
gist: A newly described ~150-million-year-old avialan, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, had teeth, short wings and a predatory foot claw suited to land rather than flight, challenging the view that bird evolution steadily favored flight and suggesting flight may have evolved multiple times.

insights.claim: Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, a bird species that lived around 150 million years ago, had sharp teeth, relatively short wings and a foot claw for attacking, and experts believe it may not have been able to fly.
insights.so_what: Pure science; no direct market angle.
insights.speaker: David Nield

insights.claim: Despite its land-adapted, dinosaur-like body, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis has bird-like features placing it in Avialae, challenging the traditional view that natural selection steadily prioritized flight traits and suggesting flight may have evolved multiple times.
insights.speaker: David Nield
